# Proof that standard relative Weyl subgroups are generated by simple reflections

Author: Worker 39.

Module `Langlands.GroupScheme.Rational.StandardRelativeWeylGenerationProof`.

## Result

`Langlands.GroupScheme.standardRelativeWeylGeneration` has type exactly
`StandardRelativeWeylGenerationStatement.{u}`, the published proposition of
`Langlands.GroupScheme.Rational.TitsStandardParabolicStatement`, at an arbitrary
universe `u`. The theorem covers every field `k : Type u`, every `G` with
`IsConnectedReductive G`, every `i : T.toGrp ⟶ G` with `IsMaximalSplitTorus i`, every
cocharacter `ν` with `IsGenericCocharacter i ν` and every `J ⊆ simpleRelativeRoots i ν`.
For all of these it proves

`Subgroup.closure (relativeReflections i J) = standardRelativeWeylGroup i ν J`.

Here `relativeReflections i J` is the set of elements of `relativeWeylGroup i = N(k)/Z(k)`
whose action on `relativeRootSpan i` is a reflection in a root of `J`. The subgroup
`standardRelativeWeylGroup i ν J` is the image in `N(k)/Z(k)` of the normalizing points
lying in the standard Levi `L_J(k)`. This is Borel–Tits (1965) 5.17: `W_Θ` is generated
by the fundamental reflections `r_a`, `a ∈ Θ`, and it is the relative Weyl group of `Z_Θ`.

No splitness, quasi-splitness, perfectness, characteristic or local-field hypothesis is
added, and nothing structural is assumed. The proof covers:

- `J = ∅`, where the theorem says `standardRelativeWeylGroup i ν ∅ = ⊥`;
- semisimple `k`-rank zero, where `J = ∅` is the only admissible set;
- nonreduced relative root systems.

The only axioms used are `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

## Implemented proof

The proof is a single term that composes published Library theorems:

```
standardRelativeWeylGenerationStatement_of_relativeWeylCoxeter
  (RootGeneratedCentralizerStructuralPremises.relativeWeylCoxeter
    ⟨relativeRootSystemStatement_of_rootRankOneFactorizationStatement rootRankOneFactorization,
      rootRankOneFactorization⟩)
```

Each step uses one published result.

1. **Rank-one factorization.** `rootRankOneFactorization` (module
   `Rational.RootRankOneFactorizationProof`) proves `RootRankOneFactorizationStatement.{u}`
   with no premises. It does this by applying `rootRankOneFactorization_of_componentReductivity`
   to the published `RelativeRoot.kernelCentralizerComponentReductive`. For each relative
   root `a` and each nonidentity rational point `x` of the root subgroup of `a`, it gives
   rational points `u′, u′′` of the root subgroup of `-a` with `u′ * x * u′′ ∈ N(k)`. The
   statement also asserts uniqueness and further properties; the chain uses only this
   existence part.
2. **Relative root system.** `relativeRootSystemStatement_of_rootRankOneFactorizationStatement`
   (module `Rational.RootSystemFromFactorPairs`) takes step 1 and gives
   `RelativeRootSystemStatement.{u}`, that is, `HasRelativeRootSystem i` for every maximal
   split torus. The relative roots form a finite crystallographic, possibly nonreduced
   root pairing on `relativeRootSpan i`, the image of its Weyl group is the range of
   `relativeWeylAction i`, and that action of `N(k)/Z(k)` is faithful.
3. **Coxeter realization.** `RootGeneratedCentralizerStructuralPremises.relativeWeylCoxeter`
   (module `Rational.RootGeneratedCentralizerReduction`) takes the pair of steps 2 and 1
   and gives `RelativeWeylCoxeterStatement.{u}`. Inside it:
   - `relativeRootReflectionExistence_of_rootRankOneFactorization` turns step 1 into
     `RelativeRootReflectionExistenceStatement.{u}`. This is integral reflection data whose
     representative for each root `a` centralizes the full scheme-theoretic kernel of `a`.
   - The published abstract theorem `Langlands.Group.rootPairingWeylCoxeterStatement_proof`
     (module `Langlands.Group.RootPairingCoxeterProof`) gives the Coxeter structure on the
     Weyl group of a finite crystallographic root pairing.
   - `relativeWeylCoxeterStatement_of_rootPairingWeylCoxeterStatement` (module
     `Rational.RelativeWeylCoxeterReduction`) moves that structure to `N(k)/Z(k)`. The
     result is a Coxeter system labelled by the simple relative roots of `ν`. Its simple
     reflection of `a` acts on characters by an integral reflection in `a`. Its Coxeter
     parabolic subgroup of every finite label set `I` is
     `standardRelativeWeylGroup i ν (rootSet i ν I)`.
4. **Generation.** `standardRelativeWeylGenerationStatement_of_relativeWeylCoxeter` (module
   `Rational.StandardRelativeWeylGenerationReduction`) takes step 3 and proves the target.
   In the Coxeter realization of the finite group `N(k)/Z(k)`, every relative reflection in
   a simple root `a` is the simple reflection of `a`. Two reflections in `a` whose product
   has finite order have the same linear form. An element acting trivially on the root
   span has an empty inversion set, so it has length zero and is trivial. Hence
   `relativeReflections i J` is the set of simple reflections labelled by `J`. The
   parabolic clause of step 3 identifies the subgroup they generate with
   `standardRelativeWeylGroup i ν J`.

This module adds no mathematics of its own. It applies step 4 to step 3, which is applied
to steps 2 and 1.

## Sources and provenance

The target is Borel–Tits, *Groupes réductifs* (1965), 5.17 (printed p.101), with the
local-field version in Renard, *Représentations des groupes réductifs p-adiques*, V.4.6
(proof, printed p.120). The statement Markdown in
`Rational.TitsStandardParabolicStatement` gives these citations. The implemented route
does not follow the Borel–Tits argument. It goes through the rank-one factorization, the
integral full-kernel reflections (the Conrad–Gabber–Prasad C.2.14–C.2.15 route recorded
in the Markdown of the cited modules) and the abstract Coxeter theorem for root pairings.
